econ-env-01-c3.text: William A. Pizer; Brian Prest (2016). Prices versus Quantities with Policy Updating. NBER Working Paper No. 22379.
econ-env-01-c3.quote: A flat schedule (prices) works better when marginal benefits are relatively flat (e.g., Pizer 2003); a vertical schedule (quantities) works better when marginal benefits are relatively steep.
econ-env-01-c3.claim: If the marginal damage curve is steep (each additional ton matters a lot), quantity instruments are better, because you cap at the right level even if costs are uncertain.
